name: Huang Jianxun
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder of Guangdong Liantai Group (Shantou); former chairman of Shanghai-listed Guangdong Liantai Environmental Protection (603797)
profile: Huang Jianxun (黄建勲) is a member of the Huang family that controls Guangdong Liantai Group, a Shantou-based infrastructure, municipal construction and real-estate group founded in 1993, whose listed arm Liantai Environmental (603797.SH) runs wastewater treatment plants. He served as chairman of the listed company.
interesting_fact: Liantai Group grew out of Shantou Dahao Municipal Construction, which went to Shenzhen to build infrastructure in the special economic zone; the group later moved into wastewater-treatment PPP projects via Liantai Environmental.
notes: Very little public English info. SSE disciplinary decisions (2023/2024) named him as actual controller and then-chairman of Liantai Environmental over related-party fund use: https://www.sse.com.cn/disclosure/credibility/supervision/measures/ident/c/10762687/files/ff035baf77574dca933d5a2c3c91723d.pdf. Identity link to Hurun 'Lian Tai' inferred, not confirmed by Hurun page. Approach via company IR if at all.

name: Lu Zhilin
current_role: Director and General Manager, Guangdong OPT Machine Vision Tech Co. (688686.SH)
profile: Lu Zhilin (卢治临, b. 1983) co-founded Dongguan-based OPT Machine Vision with his brother Lu Shenglin in 2006 and has run it as general manager; he was chairman 2016-2018. OPT makes light sources, lenses, cameras and vision software for factory automation (notably consumer-electronics and lithium-battery lines) and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding OPT he ran a small clothing shop, with only a junior-college (dazhuan) education.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded the business in 2006 as Dongguan OPT Automation Technology Co., Ltd. at about age 23, alongside his brother Dr. Lu Shenglin, who serves as chairman.
notes: Low public profile; company IR (board secretary Xu Xueliang) is the realistic route. Forbes bio spells name 'Luo Zhilin' in one line.

name: Chris Ruddy
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Newsmax Inc. (NYSE: NMAX)
profile: Christopher Ruddy, a former investigative reporter at the New York Post and Pittsburgh Tribune-Review, founded Boca Raton-based Newsmax in 1998 and launched its cable channel in 2014, now among the largest US cable news networks. Newsmax listed on the NYSE in March 2025; Ruddy owns nearly a third of the shares.
interesting_fact: He started Newsmax in 1998 with a $25,000 investment from Mellon heir Richard Mellon Scaife; by 2024 the channel was the fourth-largest US news channel with ~30 million regular viewers.
deep_cut_fact: He turned down Columbia to join St. John's University's Honors Program (BA History, summa cum laude, 1987), later earned an MPP at the LSE, and as a student worked on the 'rapid response' team of Reagan's 1984 re-election campaign.
notes: High-profile media figure, accessible and frequently interviewed; route via Newsmax corporate/IR. He also speaks on energy/environment at EarthX (https://earthx.org/speaker/chris-ruddy/).

name: Ke Kangbao
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder of Dashenlin Pharmaceutical Group (603233.SH); long-time director and general manager
profile: Ke Kangbao (柯康保) co-founded Guangzhou-headquartered Dashenlin Pharmaceutical with brothers Ke Yunfeng (chairman) and Ke Jinlong; the three each held about a third. Dashenlin grew into one of China's largest pharmacy chains, with 10,000+ stores, and listed in Shanghai in 2017. He served for years as director and general manager.
interesting_fact: The brothers' first shop, the 'Shenrong Pharmacy' (参茸大药房), opened around 1993 in an open-air market on Hongqi North Road in Maoming with an investment of just over 10,000 yuan, pioneering membership cards and discount pricing.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 the three Ke brothers signed a formal 'acting-in-concert' agreement to make all major company decisions jointly, after holding near-identical 33.3% stakes since founding.
notes: Forbes bio says 'Deshenlin'; company is Dashenlin. SSE 2024 disciplinary document lists him as co-actual controller and 'then-director', so he may no longer sit on the board. Low profile; brother Ke Yunfeng is the public face. Route via company IR.

name: Li Jialin
current_role: Chairman and CEO, VSTECS Holdings Ltd. (HKEX: 856)
profile: Li Jialin (李佳林), a Tsinghua electrical-engineering graduate (BEng, MBA), co-founded VSTECS (伟仕佳杰) in 1991. The Hong Kong-listed group is one of Asia's largest IT and cloud distributors, serving China and Southeast Asia (Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia, Philippines) across consumer electronics, enterprise systems and cloud computing.
interesting_fact: VSTECS has moved from PC distribution into cloud, operating its own 'VPlus' cloud platform and enterprise/data-center systems distribution across Southeast Asia.
deep_cut_fact: He won a National Science and Technology Progress Award (third class) and is founding president of the Tsinghua PBCSF (Wudaokou) Hong Kong EMBA alumni group and permanent president of the Tsinghua Alumni Association of Hong Kong.
notes: Email is the published general contact for VSTECS Hong Kong HQ, not personal. Relevant to podcast via cloud/data-center equipment distribution in Asia. Tsinghua alumni network is a warm angle.

name: Wende L Kotouc
current_role: Director, Associated Banc-Corp (NYSE: ASB) and its bank/trust subsidiaries (since April 1, 2026)
profile: Wende Kotouc, 63, of Omaha, spent 26 years at family-controlled American National Corporation, rising to Executive Co-Chairman and CEO of American National Bank (2019-2026). When Associated Banc-Corp acquired American National in April 2026, her stake converted into ~10.6M ASB shares (~5.7%), and she joined Associated's board.
interesting_fact: The American National sale made her one of Associated Banc-Corp's largest individual shareholders, holding about 5.7% of the Wisconsin-based regional bank.
deep_cut_fact: She first joined American National as a hire in October 1999, more than a decade before joining its board in 2013, and serves on the Omaha Airport Authority board and Creighton University's Board of Trustees.
notes: Low media profile; husband John F. Kotouc was American National co-chairman/co-CEO. Omaha Airport Authority role could be an infrastructure/energy angle. Route via Associated Banc-Corp corporate secretary/IR.

name: Hong Weidong
current_role: Deceased (was chairman and general manager, Yusys Technologies 300674.SZ)
profile: Founder of Beijing-based fintech/banking-software company Yusys Technologies (宇信科技). Died on September 29, 2026; his wife and co-founder Wu Hong was elected chairman and general manager.
notes: Deceased 2026-09-29 per Yusys announcement (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-09-30/1225589731.PDF; https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20260930/c680419431.shtml). Successor: Wu Hong (吴红), co-founder and his widow.

name: Wan Zhang
current_role: Co-founder and co-controlling shareholder (~11%), Shanghai Friendess Electronic Technology (Bochu, 688188.SH)
profile: Wan Zhang (万章) is one of five co-founders of Shanghai Friendess (柏楚电子), a spin-out of Shanghai Jiao Tong University founded in 2007 that dominates China's market for fiber-laser cutting CNC control systems. The company listed on the STAR Market in 2019; the five founders jointly control it, with Wan holding about 11%.
interesting_fact: Friendess began as a student startup next to Shanghai Jiao Tong University, backed by the Shanghai university-student entrepreneurship fund, and its laser-cutting controllers became the market leader in China.
deep_cut_fact: When the company was registered on 11 Sept 2007 with 200,000 yuan of capital (half pledged by SJTU's technology-transfer center), Wan Zhang and three of the co-founders each put in just 10,000 yuan.
notes: Very low profile; could not confirm his current executive title. Chairman/public face is Tang Ye. Route via company board secretary (Zhou Zhiyu).

name: Lu Yanping
profile: Lu Yanping (陆燕平) appeared on the 2021-2022 Hurun lists with wealth from Agile Group (雅居乐), the Zhongshan-based property developer controlled by the Chen brothers, sharing the entry with Chen Zhuoxi. Her exact link to the Chen family and any current role could not be confirmed from public sources.
notes: The SEC link to Adlai Nortye (ANL) CEO looks like a bad name match: ANL's founder/CEO is Yang (Carsten) Lu (https://adlainortye.gcs-web.com/corporate-governance/board-of-directors), a different person. No public profile found for Lu Yanping; Agile is in debt restructuring. Not a good outreach target without more info.

name: Yu Yu
current_role: Co-founder, Chairwoman and executive director, Dangdang (当当网)
profile: Peggy Yu (俞渝, b. 1965, Chongqing) worked on Wall Street after an NYU MBA, then co-founded Dangdang in 1999, modelled on Amazon, which became China's largest online bookseller and listed on the NYSE in 2010 before going private in 2016. She still leads Dangdang after settling control with co-founder Li Guoqing in 2025.
interesting_fact: She came up with the idea for Dangdang while studying Amazon's rise from early 1995 as a Wall Street professional, then launched the 'Amazon of China' with Li Guoqing in 1999.
deep_cut_fact: Her first job after Beijing Foreign Studies University was as interpreter and secretary to the general manager of boiler maker Babcock & Wilcox's Beijing company; she later gave the student commencement speech for her NYU MBA class of 1992.
notes: Still publicly active (e.g. Yabuli Forum speech Feb 2025, https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_30995098). Avoid the widely covered dispute with ex-husband Li Guoqing. Babcock & Wilcox detail is a natural energy-podcast hook.

name: Liu Qing
current_role: Co-founder, 'permanent partner' and Chief People Officer, DiDi Global (stepped down as president and board director in 2024)
profile: Jean Liu (柳青, b. 1978, Beijing) spent 12 years at Goldman Sachs Asia, rising to managing director, before joining Didi Dache as COO in 2014 and serving as president for a decade. She led the 2015 Didi-Kuaidi merger and the 2016 deal that saw Uber sell its China business to Didi. Since 2024 she focuses on organisation and talent as a permanent partner.
interesting_fact: Named to the 2017 TIME 100; she and Cheng Wei got Uber to sell its China operation to Didi in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance she trained as a computer scientist: a BS in computer science from Peking University and an MS in computer science from Harvard; NYU also awarded her an honorary Doctor of Commercial Science in 2018.
notes: Role change: https://ca.news.yahoo.com/didi-co-founder-liu-steps-114321198.html. High-profile but no longer president; route via DiDi corporate communications. Didi is also active in autonomous driving (DiDi Autonomous Driving).

name: He Keneng
profile: He Keneng (何克能) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2014-2018 with wealth from 'Yimei' (real estate and chemicals), shared with Zhang Xiuyuan. The company and any current role could not be identified from public web sources.
notes: No matching public information found in English or Chinese searches; dropped off Hurun after 2018. Needs a Chinese registry check to identify 'Yimei' before any outreach.

name: Zhong Meihong
current_role: Director (audit committee member), Shenzhen Capchem Technology (300037.SZ); re-elected to 7th board Dec 2025
profile: Zhong Meihong (钟美红, b. 1967) is a chemical engineer and one of the six-person acting-in-concert controlling group of Capchem (新宙邦), a Shenzhen maker of lithium-battery electrolytes, capacitor chemicals and fluorochemicals. She was a director of the predecessor Shenzhen Capchem Chemical and rose to executive vice president before becoming a non-executive-style director in 2017. She holds about 6% of the company.
interesting_fact: Capchem is one of the world's leading suppliers of lithium-ion battery electrolyte, a key input for EVs and grid storage batteries.
deep_cut_fact: She graduated in chemical engineering from Xiangtan University in 1990 and began as production department head at Hunan Jinhai Chemical before joining Capchem's predecessor.
notes: Low public profile; chairman Qin Jiusan is the company spokesman. Energy-storage materials angle fits the podcast. Route via Capchem board secretary/IR.

name: Anthony Lyons
current_role: Co-founder, Matterhorn Capital; chairman/partner, Future Energy Solutions (LED lighting-as-a-service)
profile: Anthony Lyons (b. June 1967) is a British property investor who co-founded Matterhorn Capital with Simon Conway. The pair bought Earl's Court and Olympia for £245m in 2004 and sold them to Liberty International for £380m in 2007, and later bought the O2 Centre. Since 2012 he has backed Future Energy Solutions, an energy-efficient LED lighting business serving clients such as BP, Ford and Shell.
interesting_fact: He and Conway flipped the Earl's Court and Olympia exhibition centres, bought for £245m in 2004, to Liberty International for £380m three years later.
deep_cut_fact: An early data-centre investor: in 2011 Matterhorn put about £250m into two UK data centres, at Bury Green in Hertfordshire and Chesham in Buckinghamshire.
notes: Private; reportedly based in the Bahamas (Sunday Times 2017). Last on the Rich List in 2020. Data-centre and energy-efficiency angles fit the podcast well. No published contact email found; the Future Energy Solutions website is the only route.
